item.title: Re: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded: Thanks- that’s actually a big help. I wanted the tree to affect kids because I think of it as affecting generations. I do like the idea of going down a horror route and I hadn’t realised how self-serving this tree is. You’ve given me a lot to think about. I’d initially thought of the tree having a timid personality but now I’m thinking an angry, blunt personality would be better. Thanks for the critique and you have a good day too!

item.title: Re: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded:
You're sort of approaching this one from the wrong angle: It sounds like the tree is using the kids to promote eco-friendly beliefs. The kids see the tree and it implants a compulsion that the kids then act on, with the moss being the way it communicates.

This places it in the category of cognitohazard, where the tree is using a sense (the sight of the moss) to manipulate the kids. Even if that manipulation has a good intention, The Foundation tends to take a dim view of SCPs that psychically manipulate people. As such, your hook should be "Well-intentioned tree becomes a force in local politics to better the environment, forcing a moral conflict between its good intentions and the way it's doing it."

That creates a much stronger narrative and shifts the tree from being "just interesting" and "very interesting". It also forces The Foundation to make some interesting choices, especially considering how hard it is to move the tree. Do they attempt to chop it down in order to neutralize it, fence it off and allow it to live, or something else?

There's also the question if the moss retains it ability to affect the kids if it is removed from the tree, and if the tree can see through the moss. If it does, then it could be the start of a new druidic cult of sorts.

Regardless, you have a good start. Now have some fun with it!

item.title: Re: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded:
Why the tree would want children to protect it even after it has adquired information about whats happening to the world? The best course of action would be try to influenciate important people, like company managers or political partys.

I don't know, I think you're trying to explain a behavir, that should even be about our survival, using an SCP. Like its not normal. Thats an approach you should be careful with.

But I really like the eggoistic self survival persona you gave to the tree, since it made a contract with the foundation to be protected and not in behalf of any other plant.

I would suggest giving it a more horror like style. It could be inside a forest, and all the other trees could have been people. If you still want to maintain that enviromental idea, it would even make more sence if transforms people into other trees since its reducing the number of humans that it ostracize and also reflorestating.

The trees could even bleed if they are cut.

Have a great day!

item.title: Sentient, climate-conscious tree
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Dunno

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tree that is intelligent and sentient and has an effect on kids and teens that come into direct contact with it that causes them to be protective of it and environmentally conscious. A small number of these young people are able to communicate with it by writing on its branches or trunk and receiving a reply written in moss that only they can interpret. It caused a month long strike by these affected youths that the foundation struggled to break up.

Central Narrative: The tree became anomalous in the late 1800s when the industrial revolution was pumping out pollution. It became more active in the past few decades after it was told by affected kids about climate change and deforestation and so on. The tree is pretty angry and upset at all this so when someone decides to cut it down to build on the land, the tree goes into full rage mode and for four straight weeks all affected kids surrounded the tree and refused to move, not even to eat or sleep though they had no symptoms of death from this. The tree eventually chills out after the foundation uses one of kids as a messenger to talk with it and promise (on behalf of the foundation) to look after it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Poor tree doesn’t want to die. Makes sure everyone knows it.

Additional Notes: Criticise away!
